I wanted to warmly thank the veterinary assistants at this clinic who were such a great help to me after the sudden loss of my best friend, Fripouille, at the beginning of September. When a pet dies, we can sometimes feel lost regarding the procedures to follow concerning their remains, what to do afterward, and thanks to them and their kindness and compassion, I was comforted knowing that my pet was well cared for and respected. Not all institutions in Paris were as kind to me when I was trying to figure out how to honor my cat and what to do with her body.

On the contrary, this clinic reassured me over the phone and was incredibly kind in guiding me and my family through this painful ordeal. Thank you also to their Animacare service, which is very respectful of animals, and for the delivery of the urn, which was very well done. If I had just one suggestion, it would be that the packaging for returning the urn could be more discreet. It makes me laugh now, but on the day itself, the veterinary assistants (who were absolutely lovely, by the way, so kind) didn't have many bags available besides a bag of Ziggy pet food. Looking back, it makes me smile, but it would be nice, if possible, if Animacare provided a more discreet and personal bag for taking home the urn containing the remains of our four-legged companions.

So, that was just a small point, a tiny minor drawback, that I wanted to mention.

In short, thank you to them for being so understanding, warm, and compassionate. It's a tough job, and they do it with professionalism and heart. So thank you. ✨

The entire team at this veterinary clinic is both professional and friendly. Starting with Dr. Baron, who has been treating my 17-year-old cat for several years and has always provided accurate and effective diagnoses. My cat, Muzo, is doing very well despite his age and doesn't even seem stressed when he's in his care! Dr. Baron takes the time to explain the treatments while reassuring my cat. His assistants are just as pleasant and attentive, especially Fabien. I recommend them without reservation! Thank you to them!

As a regular patient of Sevetys clinics, I expected to find the same level of service I've experienced at other practices, but it was quite the opposite.
The clinic is poorly maintained; my dog ​​managed to eat several things off the floor, both in the reception area and in the private examination room, which clearly hadn't been cleaned between patients. But most importantly, I encountered a haughty and extremely unpleasant veterinarian. She didn't listen and didn't even pay attention to my dog ​​when she was on the examination table, as she nearly fell off, and I had to get up to hold her. She also made incorrect statements during the consultation, which proved true as soon as I asked for the appropriate course of action.
Furthermore, there's an error on the claim form for my insurance company, which is causing me problems with them. I sincerely do not recommend this clinic, despite the fact that the veterinary assistants are absolutely lovely and respectful.

Today, January 23, 2026, at 6:46 AM, I called the emergency service because my cat had swallowed a 0.40 cm piece of thread. The veterinarian told me to bring my cat to the clinic on Avenue Parmentier. At 9:00 AM, I arrived at the door, and someone told me it would certainly not be possible to see my cat since they were not an emergency service and I didn't have an appointment. I expressed my confusion, given that I had called the clinic's emergency service. I have been a client for over 20 years. Furthermore, I am outraged by the attitude of one of the receptionists who started comparing a general practitioner to an emergency room and yelled at me when I began to get angry, telling me that they were not an emergency service.

Furthermore, I don't understand how a receptionist could behave in such a way towards a 75-year-old woman who is distraught over her cat's condition.

As you can see, I will no longer be coming to your establishment; it will be an annual loss of €2,000 for you between veterinary care and food, as my cat has kidney problems.

Having been a regular and satisfied customer of this clinic until now, particularly with the impeccable care provided by Dr. Baron, I was very disappointed during my last emergency visit on November 20th. Seen by Dr. Gaignet, I encountered a cold doctor, closed to dialogue, with no listening skills whatsoever and a severe lack of empathy.

Despite my concerns about my cat possibly having hypertension, she didn't even bother to check his blood pressure. This is absurd, given the serious risks to our animals. I had also sent her an ultrasound done a month prior, which she was supposed to review, but a week later, I still haven't received any feedback. At €145 for a consultation (including blood work), this is unacceptable and unprofessional.

However, I would like to commend the professionalism of the veterinary assistants, who were always helpful and attentive, despite the doctor's inappropriate behavior towards them in front of the clients.

If you want a serious diagnosis and rigorous follow-up, I advise you to look for another clinic or make an appointment with one of these associates.
